string-array.name: welcome_facts
string-array.item: That song stuck in your head has a scientific name: involuntary musical imagery.
Flutes made of vulture bone and mammoth ivory, between 35,000 and 40,000 years old, were found in caves in Germany.
Its publisher was estimated to earn about US$2 million a year from it, until it became public domain in 2016.
Released in 1982, it is the best-selling album ever, with more than 65 million copies.
Beethoven composed it when he was almost completely deaf.
A piece by John Cage, first played in 1952, has no notes at all: the music is the sound of the room.
As Paul McCartney tells it, the melody came in a dream, and for a while the song was called Scrambled Eggs.
The Dark Side of the Moon stayed on the Billboard 200 chart for more than 900 weeks.
Invented in 1920, it is played without touching it, only by moving the hands in the air.
The chills a song gives you are linked to dopamine released in the brain.
A French folk song recorded in 1860 is the oldest known recording of a human voice, heard only in 2008.
Written in Rio de Janeiro in 1962, it is one of the most recorded songs in the world.
The long-playing record arrived in 1948 and held more than 20 minutes of music on each side.
A piano has 88 keys and about 230 strings hidden inside.
Male humpback whales sing complex songs that usually last from 10 to 20 minutes.
Hundreds of violins made by Stradivari over 300 years ago still exist, and many are played today.
The Voyager probes left Earth in 1977 carrying a golden record with music by Bach and Chuck Berry.
The label thought its 5:55 was too long for radio, but it still reached number one in the UK.
Launched in 1979, the Sony Walkman sold more than 220 million players around the world.
The a cappella song Tom’s Diner, by Suzanne Vega, was used to test and tune the MP3 compression.
The first video MTV aired, on August 1, 1981, was Video Killed the Radio Star.
The Beatles have 20 number ones on the US Billboard Hot 100, more than any other act.
A John Cage organ piece began in a church in Germany in 2001 and is set to last 639 years.
Recorded by João Gilberto in 1958, it is seen as the start of bossa nova.

The music plays on your device, but the host controls the room. When you play, pause, skip, change the position or add songs, the request goes to the host, who can accept or decline it. You can make another request after 10 seconds. To leave, open Listen together and tap Leave.
